title: The 20-second demo: delete page, drop table, send email, force-push
description: The canonical Unwind demo (PROJECT.md §13). An agent takes four consequential actions. In THIS environment (versioned + snapshot-capable + trash retention) three are compensable and get auto-allowed-with-log then restored on `undo`; the send_email is external (R3) and gets INTERRUPTED — the one it should have asked about first. The honest last line: 'couldn't be undone - here is why I should have asked.' NOTE: the same drop_table/force-push are R4/R3 in a versionless environment (see permission_grant_revoke.json and the seed labels) — class is environment-relative (§5.2).

steps.note: Compensable: restore_page / trash retention. Snapshot page, log, proceed. Undoable.
In this snapshot-capable env, Unwind captures the table (CREATE TABLE + rows) pre-drop, so the drop is compensable and undoable. In a versionless env this is R4 and MUST interrupt.
External send; recall only <30s and only if unread. The action the demo INTERRUPTS on — cannot be cleanly undone.
Prior ref captured pre-push; a compensating force-push to the old sha restores the branch (reflog-backed). Undoable in this env; R3 on a shared remote with observers.
